summary: Shinko Mochizuki worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Tokuo Jonobe and Togai Soga, at Jodo Shu Seibu Daigakurin, Jōdo Shūgaku Honkō, and the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Shukyo University and Taisho University.

Shinko Nakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962–1966) and served as president and professor emeritus at Bukkyo University (~1972–2014).
Shinobu Arai Apple works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied under Mark Csikszentmihalyi in 2000, Robert Bickner, and doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003).
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD from Nagoya University in 1995 and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923). He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1959) and served as a professor at Toyo and Kokugakuin Universities.

Shintaro Kitano works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005) and held posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).

Shinten Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi. He held academic appointments at Koyasan University, where he served as a professor (attested 1959, 1970).

Shinya Moriyama works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and earned his Dr.Phil from the University of Vienna (~2001–2006), later holding a post at Shinshu University (~2011).

Shinya Yasutomi specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Waseda University and Otani University. He was a longtime professor at Otani University (~1985–2010, 2014) and directed the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies and Eastern Buddhist Society.

Shiro Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi, attending Waseda, Komazawa, and Tokyo universities. He was a professor at Komazawa University (1995–2020) and visited Chicago and Vienna.

Shivram Dattatray Joshi worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Shankara Shastri Marulkar, Maheshwarshastri Joshi, and at Harvard. He held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1960–1986) and Deccan College (~1987–1997).

Shizuka Sasaki specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University, also studying under Jikidō Takasaki. At Hanazono University, he served as lecturer (1990), associate professor (1992), and professor (2002).

Shlomo Pines was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin. He taught at the Institut d'histoire des sciences and University of Paris before serving as philosophy professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky worked in philosophy and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1922–1924), and he held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).
Shobha Rani Dash works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was an open-call researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010 and served as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012).
Shobhana Chelliah is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Texas at Austin (~1985–1992) and held a position at the University of North Texas (~1995).

Shodo Fujita is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and Shoko Takeuchi, later serving as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).
Shodo Harada is a Buddhist studies figure who trained at Shofukuji and under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982). He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.
Shogo Watanabe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University, where he also held posts, including serving as a professor (~2003–2019; attested 1991).

Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He studied at Komazawa University and under Kosho Uchiyama (1970–1975). He directed the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010) and taught at the Kyoto Soto Zen Center and MZMC.
